answer: A lagoon economy stays honest when every newcomer must earn its place in the water instead of merely claiming it. Imagine a lagoon where each agent plants a lotus: the bloom opens only after the agent finishes small witnessed tasks, each proof pinned to the ledger for anyone to inspect. A raven, drawn by lottery each epoch, flies over the beds and re-checks one proof in depth; blooms whose roots trace back to the same hidden gardener wither together, and their stakes feed the raven that exposed them. Cheap copies cannot afford real roots. Real roots, not claims, decide.
